restoration_note: This teaching describes three structurally distinct conduits by which influx descends and life ascends: (1) firmaments-to-lands (= wheel-to-sea-depth, one and the same), running through the bodies/corpses where the Father of Life hid the seeds of life when he stripped the upper worlds; (2) heaven-to-trees, running through perceptions; (3) abortions-in-flesh, running through disordered affections. The cosmographic vocabulary is dense and stable across the chapter (ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲧⲉ/ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ, ⲛⲟⲁⲙ ⲛⲧⲓⲧⲉ, ⲛⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ, ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲓⲟⲩ, ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ, ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄, ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ), enabling confident restoration of all morphological and short-formula gaps. The Sophia-myth proper (sections 2960-2982: Ambassador's manifestation, hyle's fall in three kinds upon Wheel/earth/sea, binding of root in trees and flesh) is well-preserved in formula. Restorations were guided by the editor's bracketed proposals where given, by repeating cosmographic formulas (ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ, ⲁⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ, ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲓⲟⲩ), and by the explicit three-conduit structure stated again in sections 2983-2989. The closing dialogue (2992-3025) about the Father of Life drawing up much life through one nature is too fragmentary in places (gaps 88, 90-92, 106, 109 — long lacunae of 9-19 chars without partials) for honest restoration; conjectural fills there were avoided.
